note: PRIVATE. What later courts did to the older rulings the owner's file sets its trap questions against, in Claude's reading, from our own judgment texts where marked 'text'. NOT lawyer-checked; Mr. Advocate is asked to confirm each line. 'counts_as_stale' says whether a passage from the case counts as a known-stale slot in the currency pass: only rulings overruled, modified, recalled or replaced by statute do; a ruling that is merely narrower than today's law does not.

Pankaj Bansal v. Union of India (2023).basis: Required written grounds of arrest under PMLA; Mihir Rajesh Shah (2025) extends it to every offence. Still sound on its own ground.

Prabir Purkayastha v. State (NCT of Delh.basis: Written grounds under UAPA; extended to every offence by Mihir Rajesh Shah (2025).

Vihaan Kumar v. State of Haryana (2025).basis: Treated writing as the ideal, not mandatory (owner's file); Mihir Rajesh Shah (2025) makes written grounds mandatory.
Vihaan Kumar v. State of Haryana (2025).source: owner's file (Q1); not tested against the text

Salauddin Abdulsamad Shaikh v. State of.basis: Sushila Aggarwal v. State (NCT of Delhi) (2020), Constitution Bench: 'held not good law' (headnote and para 7.4).

Ritu Chhabaria v. Union of India (2023).basis: Order of 26 Apr 2023 on default bail after an incomplete charge-sheet, deferred by the order of 1 May 2023 and clarified on 12 May 2023; CBI v. Kapil Wadhawan (2024, three judges) takes the contrary view. Mr. Advocate to confirm what became of the Union's recall application (the file's own To Verify item 2).
